status: extensible: any number may apply to one direction, and each must define an expression under all three primaries

sharedMeasurements.chromaticColor: A foundation, primary, secondary or accent color with C above the neutral chroma ceiling (0.04).
sharedMeasurements.coreChromaticColor: A chromatic foundation, primary or secondary color. Accents are excluded.
sharedMeasurements.chromaWeight: Declared area multiplied by C. Near-neutral grounds cover a lot of area but contribute little hue, and this weighting reflects that.

classifications.label: Warm
classifications.definition: Chroma-weighted color leans toward reds, oranges and yellows.

test.description: Share of chromaWeight inside the warm hue arc is >= minShare. Every role color except the accent counts when C >= 0.01, so a small accent cannot set the temperature of a palette.

classifications.evidence: convention: the warm/cool split is a long-standing convention, and these arc boundaries are a project decision

expressions.neutral: Off-whites, taupes and warm blacks tinted toward yellow or red.
expressions.light-vibrant: Reds, oranges or golds lead on a light ground.
expressions.dark-vibrant: Embers, oxbloods or ambers lead on a dark ground.

classifications.label: Cool
classifications.definition: Chroma-weighted color leans toward cyans, blues and blue-violets.

test.description: Share of chromaWeight inside the cool hue arc is >= minShare. Every role color except the accent counts when C >= 0.01, so a small accent cannot set the temperature of a palette.

classifications.evidence: convention: the warm/cool split is a long-standing convention, and these arc boundaries are a project decision

expressions.light-vibrant: Blues or teals lead on a light ground.
expressions.dark-vibrant: Electric blues or cyans lead on a dark ground.

classifications.label: Monochromatic
classifications.definition: Every visibly hued color belongs to one hue family and varies mainly in lightness and chroma.

test.description: The smallest hue arc containing all role colors with C >= 0.01 is <= maxArc degrees.

classifications.evidence: convention: the concept is standard, and the arc width is a project decision

expressions.neutral: One tint family runs from the foundation through to the ink.
expressions.light-vibrant: One saturated hue and its tints sit on a light ground.
expressions.dark-vibrant: One saturated hue and its shades sit on a dark ground.

classifications.label: Analogous

test.description: At least two core chromatic colors exist and their smallest containing hue arc is between minArc and maxArc degrees.

classifications.evidence: convention: the concept is standard, and the arc width is a project decision

expressions.neutral: Tinted neutrals drift between adjacent hues, such as taupe toward olive.
expressions.light-vibrant: Neighboring saturated hues sit on a light ground.
expressions.dark-vibrant: Neighboring saturated hues glow on a dark ground.

classifications.label: Complementary
classifications.definition: At least two chromatic colors sit roughly opposite each other in hue.

test.description: Some pair of chromatic colors differs in hue by at least minDifference degrees.

classifications.evidence: convention: OKLCH opposites differ from RYB or HSL opposites, so only OKLCH hue angles are used here

expressions.neutral: A small accent opposes the tint direction of the neutrals, such as a cool accent on warm neutrals.
expressions.light-vibrant: Opposed hues on a light ground, with one clearly dominant.
expressions.dark-vibrant: Opposed hues on a dark ground, with one clearly dominant.

classifications.label: Pastel
classifications.definition: Chromatic colors are predominantly very light and gentle.

test.description: At least minShare of non-foundation chromatic area has L >= minLightness and C <= maxChroma.

classifications.evidence: convention: the concept is standard, and the thresholds are a project decision

expressions.neutral: Pale tints appear only as an accent within the Neutral area budget.
expressions.light-vibrant: Pale fields are anchored by one more saturated color.
expressions.dark-vibrant: Pale colors act as the luminous figures against a dark ground.

classifications.label: Jewel Tones
classifications.definition: Deep colors held close to the sRGB limit for their lightness, like emerald, sapphire, ruby and amethyst.

test.description: At least one chromatic color has L in the range, relative chroma >= minRelativeChroma and C >= minChroma.

classifications.evidence: convention: thresholds were checked against reference emerald, sapphire, ruby and amethyst values

expressions.neutral: One deep jewel accent within the Neutral area budget.
expressions.light-vibrant: Deep saturated figures on a light ground.
expressions.dark-vibrant: A deep saturated field or figures on a darker ground.

classifications.label: Muted
classifications.definition: Most chromatic area is held well inside the available gamut.

test.description: At least minShare of non-foundation chromatic area has relative chroma below maxRelativeChroma. Foundations are excluded so a pale tinted ground cannot make bright figures count as muted.

classifications.evidence: project decision: muted describes restraint and implies nothing about quality

expressions.light-vibrant: Mostly softened color on a light ground, with one vibrant anchor.
expressions.dark-vibrant: Mostly softened color on a dark ground, with one vibrant anchor.

classifications.label: High Contrast
classifications.definition: The main figures separate strongly from the foundation.

test.description: The primary has contrast >= minPrimaryRatio on the foundation AND at least minShare of primary, secondary and accent area has contrast >= minFigureRatio on it.

classifications.evidence: project decision built on the WCAG contrast formula

expressions.neutral: Near-black against near-white, with few middle grays.
expressions.light-vibrant: Deep saturated figures on a light ground.
expressions.dark-vibrant: Bright saturated figures on a dark ground.

classifications.label: Earthy
classifications.definition: Colors recall soil, clay, stone, bark, ochre and moss.

test.description: At least minShare of chromatic area falls inside the hue arc, lightness range and chroma range. A curator confirms the result, because the numbers alone cannot establish the reference.

expressions.light-vibrant: Clay or ochre figures on a sand or oat ground.
expressions.dark-vibrant: Ember or ochre figures on an umber ground.

classifications.label: Playful
classifications.definition: An intentionally informal character created by unexpected pairings, multiple bold colors or a light touch in how color is distributed.

test.description: No numeric test. A curator assigns this and records why.

classifications.evidence: interpretation: this makes no claim that a color property causes playfulness

expressions.neutral: Wit comes from composition and one surprising accent.
expressions.light-vibrant: Several bold colors in unexpected pairings on a light ground.
expressions.dark-vibrant: Bright, candy-like figures on a dark ground.

classifications.label: Color Blocking
classifications.definition: Large, flat, adjacent fields of distinct color form the composition.

test.description: At least minBlocks foundation, primary, secondary or accent colors each occupy >= minArea of declared area and usage.flatBlocks is true. A curator confirms the result.

classifications.evidence: convention: this describes how color is distributed rather than which colors are used

expressions.neutral: Large flat planes of black, white and gray.
expressions.light-vibrant: Saturated planes adjoin white or tinted-white planes.
